scope: Targeted Phase 5 extraction from the official Amonkhet / Hour of Devastation Magic Story episodes (2017-04-05 to 2017-07-26), mostly from the official episode recap paragraphs plus short narrated passages. Not an exhaustive reading.

claims.subject: gatewatch

quotes.quote: Five Planeswalkers have come to Amonkhet to slay a dragon.
the dragon Planeswalker Nicol Bolas was perhaps the greatest such threat. So they came to Amonkhet

claims.summary: The five Gatewatch members come to Amonkhet to slay Nicol Bolas.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: the twin curving horns of Nicol Bolas—the so-called God-Pharaoh—stood as a reminder of Gideon's purpose here
"Hail, Nicol Bolas, God-Pharaoh of Amonkhet!"

claims.summary: On Amonkhet Nicol Bolas is the God-Pharaoh.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: Nissa discovered hints of Amonkhet's past, a history Nicol Bolas has overwritten.

claims.summary: Bolas has overwritten Amonkhet's past (official recap).

claims.subject: liliana_vess

quotes.quote: She came to the plane to find—and kill—another of her demon creditors.

claims.summary: Liliana came to Amonkhet to kill another of her demon creditors.

claims.subject: liliana_vess

quotes.quote: "I killed Kothophed and Griselbrand," Liliana replied with a ghost of a smile.

claims.summary: Liliana says she has already killed Kothophed and Griselbrand.
claims.limitation: Liliana's own statement to Razaketh; the killings happened in earlier arcs and are not narrated here.

claims.subject: liliana_vess

quotes.quote: Without hesitation or humanity, her two dozen selves consumed the last of the demon Razaketh.

claims.summary: Through two dozen undead crocodiles, Liliana devours the demon Razaketh.

claims.subject: kefnet

quotes.quote: Now she seeks answers from the God of Knowledge, hoping Kefnet can explain the veneer that seems to obscure the plane.

claims.summary: Kefnet is Amonkhet's God of Knowledge.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: The God-Pharaoh has returned, and the five Hours have arrived as foretold.

claims.summary: The God-Pharaoh returns and the five Hours arrive (official recap).

claims.subject: bontu

quotes.quote: Bontu strode forward and knelt in supplication to the God-Pharaoh.

claims.summary: Bontu kneels to Bolas as the God-Pharaoh.

claims.subject: hazoret

quotes.quote: The name Bontu had uttered—Nicol Bolas—had sent another searing pain through Hazoret's head, and she was now certain: some magic was suppressing her memories.

claims.summary: The name Nicol Bolas pains Hazoret, who realises magic is suppressing her memories.
claims.limitation: Hazoret concludes that some magic suppresses her memories; the text does not here say Bolas cast it.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: "No, master, I did not doubt. I was . . . delayed. You defeated them as quickly as you predicted."
The planar bridge was his. The army was ready. The Gatewatch was loose in the Multiverse.

claims.summary: Bolas defeats the Gatewatch on Amonkhet; the survivors scatter into the Multiverse.

claims.subject: chandra_nalaar

quotes.quote: Chandra couldn't find Gideon. She couldn't save Nissa. She couldn't beat the dragon.
She planeswalked away in a fiery blaze, the only trace left of her presence the blood that stained the broken rocks as it, too, evaporated under the fiery heat.

claims.summary: Chandra planeswalks away from the losing fight.

claims.subject: gideon_jura

quotes.quote: Bolas did not think Gideon's choice mattered. In the end, it was the dragon's indifference that settled his choice.
He willed his body through the Blind Eternities, the hole the dragon left in his shoulder only the most visible of his wounds.

claims.summary: Wounded, Gideon leaves Amonkhet through the Blind Eternities.

claims.subject: tezzeret

quotes.quote: Tezzeret had served him long enough to know the right answer.

claims.summary: Tezzeret arrives on Amonkhet as Bolas's servant.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: The planar bridge was his. The army was ready.

claims.summary: Bolas now has the Planar Bridge and an army ready (the Amonkhet Eternals, per later arcs).
claims.limitation: The 'army' is not named in this quote; identifying it with the Eternals is left to later packs.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: "Later. Go and tell Ral Zarek to come to me. His progress is too slow."

claims.summary: Bolas sends Tezzeret to fetch Ral Zarek, whose (unnamed) work is too slow, foreshadowing War of the Spark.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: Several decades ago he had come to the world of Amonkhet, a blighted, superstitious backworld of interest to no one who mattered
He had wrought well in his creation sixty years ago.

claims.summary: Bolas came to Amonkhet decades before the story and shaped its present order around sixty years earlier.
claims.limitation: 'Several decades' and 'sixty years ago' are Bolas's point-of-view narration relative to the story; kept as relative dates, not absolute years.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: The wise and benevolent God-Pharaoh, said to be busy preparing the wondrous afterlife for the worthy, is actually Nicol Bolas, the malevolent dragon Planeswalker whose schemes reach far beyond this plane.

claims.summary: The official plane page states that Amonkhet's God-Pharaoh is actually Nicol Bolas.
claims.limitation: Object is the plane; the precise relation is 'God-Pharaoh of Amonkhet'.

claims.subject: amonkhet_trials

quotes.quote: Each god oversees one of the five trials and instructs the initiates who are preparing to face the trial, helping them to cultivate one of the five aspects of mortal perfection: solidarity, knowledge, strength, ambition, and zeal.

claims.summary: Each of Amonkhet's five gods oversees one of five trials: solidarity, knowledge, strength, ambition and zeal.

claims.subject: nissa_revane

quotes.quote: Determined to uncover Nicol Bolas's intentions with the plane, Nissa and Chandra explore the city in search of answers.

claims.summary: Nissa and Chandra explore Naktamun to uncover Bolas's intentions for Amonkhet.

claims.subject: curse_of_wandering

quotes.quote: Those that die will always return. That is the Curse of Wandering.

claims.summary: On Amonkhet the dead always rise again; this is the Curse of Wandering.
claims.limitation: Revealed to Nissa as a vision of the plane's own voice, not narrated as a general rule.

claims.subject: gideon_jura

quotes.quote: I walked quietly along the path, following in the wake of Oketra.
While Gideon Jura had many lingering questions about the world, the presence of the divine most captured his attention and curiosity.

claims.summary: Gideon walks through Naktamun in the wake of the god Oketra.

claims.subject: samut

quotes.quote: Years before the arrival of the Gatewatch on Amonkhet, the fate and future of three children had unforeseen effects on the destiny of the plane.
Even though they were the same age, Samut stood nearly a head taller than Nakht.

claims.summary: Years before the Gatewatch arrived, Samut and the young aven Nakht grew up together.
claims.limitation: 'Friend' is inferred from the scene; the third child (Djeru) is not modelled in this claim.

claims.subject: samut

quotes.quote: After discovering that her city is not the way it was only decades ago, she is determined to convince her oldest and dearest friend, Djeru, to believe her.

claims.summary: Djeru is Samut's oldest and dearest friend; she tries to convince him the city has been changed.

claims.subject: samut

quotes.quote: She has spent the last few days on the run and is desperate to stay alive long enough to face the trespasser who transformed her world.

claims.summary: Samut, a fugitive, wants to survive long enough to face 'the trespasser' who transformed her world.
claims.limitation: The trespasser is Bolas (the God-Pharaoh) by context; this episode's recap does not name him.

claims.subject: nicol_bolas

quotes.quote: There was just enough time left to put into place the possible means to regain his godhood.
The gods of Amonkhet saw the dragon hovering outside the protection of the Hekma.

claims.summary: The dragon arriving at Amonkhet has only days to set up the means to regain his godhood.
claims.limitation: The dragon is unnamed in the quoted lines; identification with Bolas comes from the arc.

claims.subject: hazoret

quotes.quote: As he joined his sister Hazoret at the banks of the Luxa, Rhonas felt an uncharacteristic chill permeate his scales.

claims.summary: Hazoret is Rhonas's sister.

claims.subject: rhonas

quotes.quote: Rhonas pulled his staff back, and the scorpion god fell to its knees, still chittering weakly.

claims.summary: Rhonas battles the scorpion god at the Hour of Glory.

claims.subject: locust_god

quotes.quote: And so the great locust god fulfilled the great promise, and thus the Hekma was torn asunder, its protections cast aside before the return of the God-Pharaoh.

claims.summary: The locust god tears the Hekma asunder at the Hour of Promise.
claims.limitation: Quoted from the in-world scripture epigraph that opens the episode, not plain narration.

claims.subject: hapatra

quotes.quote: Hapatra stood on the steps of the Temple of Strength, watching the blood of the Luxa seep upriver, transforming the water to crimson as its stain spread.
She wished she could stand alongside Rhonas to greet the newcomers, but the viziers had agreed in the moment that it was best to stay at their temples.

claims.summary: Hapatra is a vizier at Rhonas's Temple of Strength.
claims.limitation: That the Temple of Strength is Rhonas's is inferred from the episode, not stated in these lines.

claims.subject: hazoret

quotes.quote: "Hazoret asked that Djeru and I protect those we could—to hide among the desert sands.
She and Djeru had obeyed the god, parting ways with Hazoret and striking out toward the edges of the city.

claims.summary: Hazoret tells Samut and Djeru to protect the survivors and flee into the desert.

remaining: Every AKH/HOU episode is now cited, mostly with one or two claims; Samut's spark, the deaths of Oketra and Kefnet, and the full Hours sequence are not modelled
Nakht's and Djeru's later fates, and the Trials' structure, are not graded
Scripture epigraphs are graded IMPLIED with a limitation; they are in-world texts, not narration
